_comment: Scope-containment conformance vector (v1), per spec docs/spec/scope.md S.3 and ADR-0005. ADDITIVE AND SIGNATURE-FREE: containment is a PREDICATE OVER a document, never part of one, so this vector introduces no signed field, no encoding rule and no digest. mint_v1.json, mint_pop_v1.json, chain_v1.json and attestation_v1.json are untouched and are NOT re-frozen by this vector's existence -- verified: no verdict in chain_v1.json changes under this rule. A conforming implementation MUST, for each case, return `expected` from its single scope matcher (Rust `scope_contains`, Python `scope_contains`, TypeScript `scopeContains`). This is the FIRST vector to police the matcher: before 0.5.0 the three implementations agreed only by review, which is how bare prefix matching survived in all three at once.

rule.statement: An entry P contains a resource R iff R == P, or P ends with a separator and R starts with P, or R starts with P followed by a separator. An empty boundary list is unrestricted. Bare prefix matching is NOT containment.
rule.segment_constraint: A scope segment MUST NOT contain a separator (S.2). This constraint is what makes honouring both separators safe rather than widening. It is normative on producers and NOT enforced by the matcher in 0.5.0 (S.6).

cases.why: empty boundary is unrestricted (top)
empty boundary admits the empty resource
an entry contains itself
dot-separated child
REGRESSION: hyphenated sibling is NOT contained
REGRESSION: bare textual prefix is NOT containment
REGRESSION: digit-suffixed sibling is NOT contained
slash-separated child
REGRESSION: slash-namespace hyphenated sibling
both separators honoured: '.' is a separator by fiat (S.2)
both separators honoured: '/' after a slash-namespace entry
no separator at the boundary is not containment
trailing-separator entry matches by plain prefix
trailing-separator entry still requires the separator
trailing slash entry matches by plain prefix
any entry may match (disjunction over the boundary)
no entry matches
multi-byte-adjacent segment, child
multi-byte-adjacent segment, sibling is NOT contained
single-segment root contains a child
REGRESSION: 'database' is not under 'data'
